title: CFDE-EXPLORE
bodyHtml:
CFDE-EXPLORE: Explore CFDE resources with your genes

Follow these steps to effectively explore CFDE resources with your genes:

  1. Input Your Genes (Choose one method to populate the Genes field):
    1. Load via Phenotype Gene Set Associations:
      • Enter your gene set associations in the format: Phenotype, Gene Set, Source (e.g., rare inborn errors of metabolism, T69-Brown-Adipose_Male_BW_Down, motrpac).
      • Click the 'Load genes' button to automatically retrieve and populate the Genes field.
    2. Enter Genes Directly:
      • Type the specific gene identifiers you want to analyze, separated by commas (e.g., TP53, BRCA1, MYC, EGFR).
  2. Optional: Enable AI Analysis Scoring

    If you wish to obtain an AI-driven relevance score for your genes:

    1. Enter Your Hypothesis:
      • Provide a brief, relevant hypothesis in the dedicated field.
  3. Explore Available Options (Requires genes to be entered in Step 1):
    1. Perform GTEx Tissue Expression Analysis:
      • Click the Open GTEx Browser button.
      • This will launch an interactive session to visualize gene expression patterns across human tissues using the official GTEx portal.
    2. Conduct MoTrPAC Exercise Response Analysis:
      • Click the Open Jupyter Notebook button.
      • Explore how your genes respond to endurance exercise across 20 tissues and 7 omics platforms in the MoTrPAC rat study using an interactive app adapted from the MoTrPAC team's R analysis notebook.
    3. Explore in Playbook Workflow Builder:
      • Click the Open Playbook Workflow builder button.
      • This opens the Playbook Workflow Builder, a tool from the CFDE Data Resource Center that performs comprehensive gene set enrichment analysis across multiple CFDE databases (e.g., GTEx Tissues V8, LINCS L1000, IDG Drug Targets) and provides interactive visualizations.
    4. Obtain Hypothesis Relevance & Innovation Scores:
      • Click the Generate scores button.
      • Generate AI-powered scores showing how relevant and novel each gene is to your specific hypothesis. This will help prioritize which genes are most important for your research.
